Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential $U$ and residual forces $d$
of the standing regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Assume the presentation is hyperregular
on its charts, with the Hamiltonians $H$ and $\widetilde H$ and inverse
Legendre branches of [[def-cm12-hamiltonian]],
[[def-cm12-hyperregularity]],
[[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]]. The momentum charts, their forms
and their canonical coordinates are those of [[def-cm13-two-form]] and
[[def-cm13-canonical-form]]; dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]] and
differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) The chart datum.** Fix one momentum chart of the presentation: either
the Cartesian chart with the coordinates $(t,x,p)$ on
$I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ and the Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] clause (a), or the chart of a
generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates, the
coordinates $(t,q,p)$ on $I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ and the
Hamiltonian $\widetilde H$ of clause (b). Write $m\in\{3N,r\}$ for the
number of momentum pairs, let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^{m}$ denote the
configuration-coordinate domain of the chart ($Q$ in the Cartesian case,
$\Omega$ in the other), and write $H$ for the corresponding Hamiltonian,

$$H:I_{0}\times V\times\mathbb R^{m}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad (t,q,p)\longmapsto H(t,q,p),$$

a function of class $C^{2}$ and dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (energy) by
[[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]]. Let $J'\subseteq I_{0}$,
$U'\subseteq V$ and $A'\subseteq\mathbb R^{m}$ be nonempty open sets
([[def-metric-topology]], [[def-interval]]).

**(b) Solutions of the equation.** A map

$$S:J'\times U'\times A'\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad (t,q,\alpha)\longmapsto S(t,q,\alpha),$$

of class $C^{3}$ **solves the Hamilton-Jacobi equation associated with $H$
on $J'\times U'\times A'$** when

$$S_{t}(t,q,\alpha)+H\bigl(t,\,q,\,S_{q}(t,q,\alpha)\bigr)=0\qquad\bigl((t,q,\alpha)\in J'\times U'\times A'\bigr),$$
where $S_{t}$ is the partial derivative in $t$ and
$S_{q}=(S_{q^{1}},\dots,S_{q^{m}})$ is the gradient in $q$
([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]); the momentum slot of $H$ is
substituted by $p=S_{q}(t,q,\alpha)$. This is exactly the mathematical
Hamilton-Jacobi equation of
[[def-cm-hamilton-jacobi-equation-and-complete-integral]] associated with
the function $H$ on the open set $J'\times U'\times\mathbb R^{m}$, read in
the chart coordinates $(t,q,p)$; the two definitions determine the same
class of functions.

**(c) Dimensions and chart consistency.** The equation forces
$[S]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (action): $S_{t}$ has dimension $[S]\tau^{-1}$
and $H$ has dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, while each $S_{q^{a}}$ has
dimension $[S]/\gamma_{a}$ with $\gamma_{a}$ the declared dimension of the
coordinate $q^{a}$ in this chart; the substitution is dimensionally
consistent in every chart because the chart momenta of
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]] have dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}\gamma_{a}^{-1}$. In the Cartesian chart all
$\gamma_{a}=\ell$ and $[S]/\ell=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$, the momentum dimension.

**(d) Status.** The equation is attached to the declared datum: replacing
the chart, the inverse Legendre branch or the potential representative
changes $H$ by the rules recorded in clause (d) of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] and hence changes the equation, and a solution
family $S$ is a solution for that datum only. The item defines a class of
functions; whether a given datum admits solutions, and how solutions
produce curves of the model, is not asserted here. In particular no
existence theorem, no global solution, no equation of motion for the model,
no conservation law and no measured value is claimed.

Adopt the datum of [[def-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-equation]]: one momentum chart
of a hyperregular potential presentation, its $C^{2}$ Hamiltonian $H$ of
dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ on $I_{0}\times V\times\mathbb R^{m}$, open
sets $J'\subseteq I_{0}$, $U'\subseteq V$ and $A'\subseteq\mathbb R^{m}$,
and a $C^{3}$ map $S:J'\times U'\times A'\to\mathbb R$ that solves the
Hamilton-Jacobi equation associated with $H$ on $J'\times U'\times A'$.
Dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]] and differentiability classes are
those of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Complete integral.** Let $(t_{0},q_{0},\alpha_{0})\in
J'\times U'\times A'$. The solution $S$ is a **complete integral of the
model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation at $(t_{0},q_{0},\alpha_{0})$** when the
mixed derivative

$$S_{q\alpha}(t,q,\alpha):=\Bigl(\frac{\partial^{2}S}{\partial q^{a}\partial\alpha_{j}}(t,q,\alpha)\Bigr)_{a,j=1}^{m}\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$$
is invertible at the base point, $\det S_{q\alpha}(t_{0},q_{0},\alpha_{0})
\ne0$ ([[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]],
[[def-invertible-euclidean-linear-map]], mixed partials being those of
[[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]]). This is exactly the
mathematical notion of a complete integral of
[[def-cm-hamilton-jacobi-equation-and-complete-integral]] applied to the
function $H$ on the chart domain $J'\times U'\times\mathbb R^{m}$.

**(b) Parameters and their dimensions.** The third variable
$\alpha=(\alpha_{1},\dots,\alpha_{m})$ is read with the declared coordinate
dimensions $\gamma_{a}$ of $q$ in the fixed chart,
$[\alpha_{j}]=\gamma_{j}$. With this reading the entries of
$S_{q\alpha}$ are dimensionless, so the nondegeneracy condition is
dimensionally meaningful and chart-consistent, and the momentum map below
carries the momentum dimension.

**(c) Momentum map and Jacobi constants.** For a complete integral $S$ the
**momentum map** and the **Jacobi constants** of $S$ are the maps

$$p(t,q,\alpha):=S_{q}(t,q,\alpha),\qquad\beta(t,q,\alpha):=S_{\alpha}(t,q,\alpha),$$
so that $p$ has the chart-momentum dimensions of
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], $[p_{a}]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}
\gamma_{a}^{-1}$, and $\beta$ has the same dimensions as $p$,
$[\beta_{j}]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}\gamma_{j}^{-1}$: the product
$\beta_{j}\,\alpha_{j}$ has the action dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ of
$S$. The pair $(\beta,\alpha)$ is the **Jacobi data** of the complete
integral at the base point.

**(d) Status.** The item defines data attached to the presentation and to
the chosen solution. It asserts neither that a complete integral exists
for a given presentation, nor that its characteristic curves are motions
of the model, nor that $\beta$ is constant along such curves; those are
the claims of the page's characteristics theorem. It also
asserts no global statement: $\det S_{q\alpha}\ne0$ is required at the
base point only, and the theorem below records its local consequences.

Let $n\ge1$, let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and
$A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty open sets, let $H:J\times U\times\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be of
class $C^2$, and let $S:J\times U\times A\to\mathbb R$ be a $C^3$ complete integral of the
Hamilton-Jacobi equation associated with $H$ at $(t_0,q_0,\alpha_0)\in J\times U\times A$
([[def-cm-hamilton-jacobi-equation-and-complete-integral]]); write $\beta_0:=S_\alpha(t_0,q_0,\alpha_0)$.
Then:

1. (characteristics) for every $\alpha$ sufficiently close to $\alpha_0$ there is an open interval
   $I_\alpha\ni t_0$ and a curve $q:I_\alpha\to U$ with $q(t_0)=q_0$ solving
   $q'(t)=H_p\bigl(t,q(t),S_q(t,q(t),\alpha)\bigr)$, and with $p(t):=S_q(t,q(t),\alpha)$ the pair
   $(q,p)$ solves Hamilton's equations $q'=H_p$, $p'=-H_q$ on $I_\alpha$;
2. (Jacobi constants) $\beta(t):=S_\alpha(t,q(t),\alpha)$ is constant on $I_\alpha$, equal to
   $S_\alpha(t_0,q_0,\alpha)$;
3. (local converse) for $(\alpha,\beta)$ near $(\alpha_0,\beta_0)$ the equation
   $\beta=S_\alpha(t,q,\alpha)$ can be solved locally for $q=Q(t,\alpha,\beta)$, and with
   $p:=S_q(t,Q(t,\alpha,\beta),\alpha)$ the curve $t\mapsto(Q,p)$ solves Hamilton's equations;
4. (canonical labels) on the domain of the local diffeomorphism $(q,p)\mapsto(\beta,\alpha)$
   obtained by composing $(q,p)\mapsto(q,\alpha)$ with $(q,\alpha)\mapsto(\beta,\alpha)$, one has
   the two-form identity $dq\wedge dp=d\beta\wedge d\alpha$ at every fixed $t$; that is,
   $(\beta,\alpha)$ are local canonical coordinates, conjugate to $(q,p)$, in which the
   $\beta$ are constants of the motion of clause 2.

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing
regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Let $H$ be the Cartesian Hamiltonian of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]], let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a generalized-coordinate map
with substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L$, kinetic metric
$G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$, substituted potential
$\widetilde U(t,q)=U(t,X(q))$ and residual generalized force
$Q^{\mathrm{res}}(t,q,v)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}d(t,X(q),DX(q)v)$, and let
$\widetilde H$ be the Hamiltonian in the coordinates $X$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]). Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a nonempty open interval
and let $x:J\to Q$ be a $C^{2}$ curve, with $p(t):=\mathsf Mx'(t)$
([[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]). Then:

1. **(potential branch)** Assume $d\equiv0$ on the state domain. The following
   are equivalent:
   (a) $x$ is a motion of the model on $J$
   ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]);
   (b) $(x,p)$ satisfies $x'(t)=H_{p}\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)$ and
   $p'(t)=-H_{x}\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)$ for every $t\in J$;
   (c) for all reals $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subseteq J$ the restriction
   $x|_{[a,b]}$ is stationary for the action $S$ of $L$ on $[a,b]$
   ([[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]],
   [[pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations]]).

2. **(residual forces)** For a $C^{2}$ curve $x:J\to Q$ with
   $p(t)=\mathsf Mx'(t)$ the following are equivalent:
   (a) $\mathsf Mx''(t)=-\nabla_{x}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+d\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)$
   for every $t\in J$;
   (b) $x'(t)=H_{p}\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)$ and
   $p'(t)=-H_{x}\bigl(t,x(t),p(t)\bigr)+d\bigl(t,x(t),\mathsf M^{-1}p(t)\bigr)$
   for every $t\in J$.

3. **(coordinate form)** Let $q:J\to\Omega$ be a $C^{2}$ curve and put
   $p(t):=G(q(t))q'(t)$. Then the declared Lagrange equations of
   [[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]] clause (e) are equivalent
   to the Hamilton system of $\widetilde H$: for every $t\in J$,

$$\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)(t)=Q^{\mathrm{res}}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ q'(t)=\widetilde H_{p}\bigl(t,q(t),p(t)\bigr),\quad p'(t)=-\widetilde H_{q}\bigl(t,q(t),p(t)\bigr)+Q^{\mathrm{res}}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr);$$

   in particular, when $d\equiv0$ the vanishing of the Lagrange operator is
   equivalent to $q'=\widetilde H_{p}$ and $p'=-\widetilde H_{q}$.

4. **(constraint elimination)** Assume in addition that $d\equiv0$ and that
   $X$ is a parametrization of a scleronomic regular holonomic-constraint
   locus in the sense of [[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]
   clause (d), with the ideal-reaction law of
   [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]]. Then the equivalent conditions of
   clause 3 with $Q^{\mathrm{res}}\equiv0$ hold for $q$ if and only if
   $x=X\circ q$ is a constrained motion of the model with an ideal reaction
   ([[pthm-cm07-lagrangian-reduction-of-ideal-constraints]]).

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation, the declared chart and, in clause 4, the constraint datum and
ideal-reaction law; it asserts no existence or uniqueness of solutions, no
conservation law and no empirical content.

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data, charts and Hamiltonian field of [[def-cm13-two-form]],
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]: masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ and open
configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ with mass operator
$\mathsf M$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]), time window $I_{0}$, $C^{2}$
potential $U$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing regularity
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-units]]), the Cartesian
Hamiltonian $H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x)$ and, for a
generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with kinetic metric
$G=DX^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX$, the chart Hamiltonian
$\widetilde H(t,q,P)=\tfrac12P\cdot G(q)^{-1}P+\widetilde U(t,q)$
([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]], [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]],
[[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]). Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a nonempty open
interval. Then:

1. **(potential branch, Cartesian chart)** Assume $d\equiv0$ on the state
   domain. For a $C^{2}$ curve $x:J\to Q$ with $p(t):=\mathsf Mx'(t)$ the
   following are equivalent: (a) $x$ is a motion of the model
   ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]); (b) $\dot x(t)=H_{p}(t,x(t),p(t))$ and
   $\dot p(t)=-H_{x}(t,x(t),p(t))$ for every $t\in J$; (c) the curve
   $t\mapsto(x(t),p(t))$ is an integral curve of the time-dependent field
   $t\mapsto X_{H_{t}}$, i.e. satisfies
   $\dot z(t)=X_{H_{t}}(z(t))$ with $z=(x,p)$
   ([[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]).
2. **(generalized-coordinate chart)** Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a
   generalized-coordinate map and let $q:J\to\Omega$ be a $C^{2}$ curve with
   $x:=X\circ q$ and $P(t):=G(q(t))q'(t)$. Then the declared Lagrange
   equations with residual generalized force,
   $\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)(t)=Q^{\mathrm{res}}(t,q(t),q'(t))$, are
   equivalent to
   $q'(t)=\widetilde H_{P}(t,q(t),P(t))$ and
   $P'(t)=-\widetilde H_{q}(t,q(t),P(t))+Q^{\mathrm{res}}(t,q(t),q'(t))$;
   in particular, when $d\equiv0$, they are equivalent to
   $(q,P)$ being an integral curve of $X_{\widetilde H_{t}}$.
3. **(residual forces, Cartesian chart)** For a $C^{2}$ curve $x:J\to Q$
   with $p=\mathsf Mx'$, the model's forced equation
   $\mathsf Mx''=-\nabla_{x}U(t,x)+d(t,x,x')$ holds on $J$ if and only if
   $\dot x=H_{p}$ and $\dot p=-H_{x}+d(t,x,\mathsf M^{-1}p)$ on $J$.
4. **(when is the forced field Hamiltonian?)** The forced field
   $(x,p)\mapsto\bigl(\mathsf M^{-1}p,-\nabla_{x}U(t,x)+d(t,x,\mathsf M^{-1}p)\bigr)$
   is the Hamiltonian field of a $C^{2}$ phase function on its domain if and
   only if there is a $C^{2}$ function $V:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ with
   $d(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x}V(t,x)$ for every $(t,x,v)$ of the state domain; in
   that case the phase function is $H+V$ up to an independently chosen
   additive $C^2$ function of $t$ on each connected component of $Q$, and the model's forced motions are the motions of the potential
   presentation $(U+V,0)$.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the declared chart; it asserts no existence or uniqueness of
solutions, no completeness, no conservation law and no empirical content.

Let a force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] be given: time window
$I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$ nondegenerate and open, configuration domain
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ open ([[def-cm01-configuration]] clause (a)),
fixed masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), and a
force map $F$ with the standing continuity and state-local-Lipschitz
hypotheses of clause (iii) of that postulate.

**(a) State domain and inverse-mass operator.** The **state domain** of the
model is

$$D:=I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3N}\times\mathbb R^{3N},$$

an open subset of $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{6N}$; a point $(t,x,v)\in D$ is a
time together with the **state** $z=(x,v)$ of positions $x\in Q$ and coordinate
velocities $v\in(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$ of the labels ([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). The **inverse-mass operator** is the linear map

$$\mathsf M^{-1}:\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \mathsf M^{-1}(u_{1},\dots,u_{N}):=\Bigl(\frac{u_{1}}{m_{1}},\dots,\frac{u_{N}}{m_{N}}\Bigr),$$

the inverse of the mass operator $\mathsf M$ of clause (d) of
[[def-cm01-configuration]].

**(b) Associated first-order system.** The **associated first-order field** of
the model is

$$\mathcal F:D\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{3N}\times\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \mathcal F(t,x,v):=\Bigl(v,\ \mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)\Bigr),$$

and the **associated first-order system** is $z'=\mathcal F(t,z)$ on the open
domain $D$, in the sense of
[[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]; here
$z=(x,v)\in\mathbb R^{6N}$. The map $\mathcal F$ satisfies the
Picard–Lindelöf hypotheses of
[[thm-picard-lindelof-local-existence-and-uniqueness]]: it is continuous on
$D$, and it is locally Lipschitz in the state variable $z$ locally uniformly
in time, because its first component $z\mapsto v$ is linear and its second is
the composition of the force map $F$ — which is locally Lipschitz in $(x,v)$
locally uniformly in time by [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iii) —
with the linear map $\mathsf M^{-1}$.

**(c) Motions.** Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior, endpoints read with one-sided derivatives as in
[[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]. A **motion** of
the model on $J$ is a curve $x:J\to Q$ of class $C^{2}$ such that
$t\in I_{0}$ for every $t\in J$ and

$$m_{i}\,\ddot x_{i}(t)=F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),\dot x(t)\bigr)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N,\ t\in J).$$

Equivalently: the state curve $z=(x,\dot x):J\to D$ is a solution of the
associated first-order system on $J$. Indeed, if $x$ is a motion then
$z=(x,x')$ is $C^{1}$ with
$z'=(x',x'')=(x',\mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,x'))=\mathcal F(t,z)$ and $z(t)\in D$;
conversely, if $z=(x,v)$ is a solution with $z(t)\in D$ for all $t$, then
$x'=v$ and $v'=\mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)$, so $v$ is $C^{1}$, $x$ is $C^{2}$, and
multiplying the second equation by the masses returns the displayed
second-order equation. Motions of the labels of the model are exactly these
curves by [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iv).

**(d) Initial data and maximal motion.** An **initial datum** of the model is
a triple $(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})$ with $t_{0}\in I_{0}$, $x_{0}\in Q$ and
$v_{0}\in(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$; write $z_{0}:=(x_{0},v_{0})$. A **maximal
motion** with this datum is a motion $x:J_{\max}\to Q$ with $x(t_{0})=x_{0}$
and $\dot x(t_{0})=v_{0}$ that has no extension to a motion of the model on a
strictly larger interval. By the Picard–Lindelöf hypotheses verified in (b)
and the maximal-solution theorem
[[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution]] (with
[[def-maximal-ode-solution]]): every initial datum has exactly one maximal
motion, its **maximal interval** $J_{\max}$ is an open interval containing
$t_{0}$ and contained in $I_{0}$, and every motion with the same datum is the
restriction of the maximal one. The restriction statement transfers from the
associated first-order system to motions through the equivalence in (c).

**(e) Newtonian flow.** The **Newtonian flow** of the model is the map

$$\Phi:\Omega\longrightarrow Q\times\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \Omega:=\bigl\{(t,t_{0},z_{0}):t_{0}\in I_{0},\ z_{0}\in Q\times\mathbb R^{3N},\ t\in J_{\max}(t_{0},z_{0})\bigr\},$$

defined by $\Phi(t;t_{0},z_{0}):=z(t)$, where $t\mapsto z(t)=(x(t),\dot x(t))$
is the state curve of the maximal motion with datum $(t_{0},z_{0})$. By (d) the
assignment is well defined: the maximal motion is unique, so $\Phi$ is a
function on $\Omega$ and not merely a relation. For fixed $t_{0}$ and $z_{0}$
the curve $t\mapsto\Phi(t;t_{0},z_{0})$ is defined exactly on the maximal
interval $J_{\max}(t_{0},z_{0})$.

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], in the
fixed inertial frame with adapted coordinates $(t,x)$ used there: $N\ge1$
labels with masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$, time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), $C^{2}$ potential $U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$
of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing
regularity ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]],
the Euclidean inner product of $\mathbb R^{3N}$ is [[def-euclidean-inner-product]],
and gradients and Jacobians are those of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]
and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

**(a) Cartesian momentum.** For a state $(t,x,v)\in I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
define the **momentum of the labels** by

$$p(t,x,v):=\mathsf M v\;=\;(m_{1}v_{1},\dots,m_{N}v_{N}),$$

whose label components are $p_{i}=m_{i}v_{i}$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]
clause (d)); its dimension is $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$ (read in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$). The space $\mathbb R^{3N}$ is
identified with its dual by the Euclidean inner product, so that $p$ is a
**covector** acting on a velocity $w$ by the dot product $p\cdot w$. The pair
$(x,p)$ is the **cotangent datum** of the state, and $I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
with coordinates $(t,x,p)$ is the **momentum phase chart** of the
presentation.

**(b) Fibre derivative.** The **fibre derivative** (the velocity Legendre
coordinate) of the presentation is $p:=\mathcal L_{v}(t,x,v)$, the Legendre
map of the fibre-full chart $(O,L)$ of clause (c) of
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], in the sense of
[[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]] (the chart data are those of
[[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]]). Because $L=K-U$ with
$K'(v)=\mathsf Mv$ and $U$ independent of the velocity slot (clause (a) of
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]), one has
$\mathcal L_{v}(t,x,v)=\mathsf Mv$: the fibre derivative and the momentum of
clause (a) are the same covector, and the Legendre map of the presentation is
$(t,x,v)\mapsto(t,x,\mathsf Mv)$.

**(c) Generalized momenta.** Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a generalized-coordinate
map of the model, with substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L$, substituted
potential $\widetilde U$ and kinetic metric $G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]] clauses (a)-(b),
[[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], [[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]]).
The **generalized momentum** of the presentation in the coordinates $X$ is
the covector

$$p(t,q,v):=\widetilde L_{v}(t,q,v)=G(q)v,$$

whose components $p_{a}=\partial\widetilde L/\partial v_{a}$ have dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}\gamma_{a}^{-1}$ (action divided by the dimension
$\gamma_{a}$ of the coordinate $q_{a}$), while the **pairing**
$p\cdot v=\sum_{a}p_{a}v^{a}$ has dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$. For the
Cartesian chart, $X=\mathrm{id}$, $\Omega=Q$, $G=\mathsf M$, and clause (c)
reduces to clause (a).

**(d) Status and warnings.** The item defines the momentum datum of a declared
presentation as a model object. It introduces no force law, no equation of
motion and no measured value; it depends on the declared chart and on the
declared coordinate dimensions $\gamma_{a}$, and it is independent of the
residual forces $d$ and of the normalization $U\mapsto U+c(t)$ of the
potential representative ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]
clause (c)). The momentum is not in general mass times coordinate velocity: in
the coordinates $X$ it is $G(q)v$, and the identity $p_{i}=m_{i}v_{i}$ is
specific to Cartesian data. The evaluation of the velocity Hessian, the
invertibility of the fiberwise momentum map, the Hamiltonian of an inverse
branch and the evolution equations are the subject of the other items of this
page, not of this definition. All differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data, charts and forms of [[def-cm13-two-form]]: masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$,
open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ and mass operator
$\mathsf M$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]), time window $I_{0}$, $C^{2}$
potential $U$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing regularity
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-units]]), the Cartesian phase
domain $W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ with $n=3N$, its canonical one-form
$\lambda$ and two-form $\omega=-d\lambda$, and for each generalized-coordinate
map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates and kinetic metric $G$ the chart map
$\Phi_{X}(q,P)=(X(q),\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}P)$ with pullbacks
$\lambda_{X}=\Phi_{X}^{*}\lambda$ and $\omega_{X}=\Phi_{X}^{*}\omega$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], [[def-cm12-hyperregularity]]). Then:

1. **(Cartesian chart)** $\omega$ is the standard two-form of the phase
   domain $W$ in the sense of
   [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]: $d\omega=0$ and
   $\omega$ is nondegenerate at every point of $W$; hence $(W,\omega)$ is a
   symplectic manifold in the sense of
   [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]].
2. **(generalized-coordinate chart)** On $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$,

$$\lambda_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}P_{a}\,dq^{a},\qquad \omega_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}dq^{a}\wedge dP_{a};$$

   consequently $\omega_{X}$ is closed and nondegenerate at every point, so
   $\Phi_{X}^{*}\omega$ is the standard two-form of the phase domain
   $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ and $\Phi_{X}$ preserves the two-form.
3. **(chart independence)** Where two of the presentation's charts are
   defined and overlap, the transition between them preserves the two-form,
   and the difference of their canonical one-forms is closed: any two
   momentum charts of the presentation describe the same symplectic
   structure on the overlap, up to the closed one-form $\lambda$ gauge.

The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the
declared presentation and the cited mathematics. It asserts no equation of
motion, no conservation law, no completeness of any flow and no empirical
content.

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
momentum charts, the phase domains and the two-form datum of
[[def-cm13-two-form]]: the Cartesian phase domain $W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
with $n=3N$, its two-form $\omega$, and for each generalized-coordinate map
$X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates the chart map $\Phi_{X}$ and the form
$\omega_{X}$ ([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], [[def-cm01-configuration]]). All
differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Canonical coordinates.** Let $W_{0}\subseteq W$ (or
$W_{0}\subseteq\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$) be nonempty open, and let

$$\theta=(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m}):W_{0}\longrightarrow V\subseteq\mathbb R^{2m}$$

be a $C^{1}$ chart of $W_{0}$ onto an open set $V$ ([[def-metric-topology]]),
with $m$ the half-dimension of $W_{0}$. The coordinates $\theta$ are
**canonical coordinates for the presentation's two-form** on $W_{0}$ when the
two-form takes the **canonical form**

$$\omega=\sum_{a=1}^{m}d\theta^{a}\wedge d\theta^{m+a}$$

on $W_{0}$ ([[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]); equivalently, when the
pullback identity $\theta^{*}\omega_{V}^{\mathrm{st}}=\omega|_{W_{0}}$ holds
for the standard two-form $\omega_{V}^{\mathrm{st}}$ of $V$
([[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]],
[[def-pullback-of-a-differential-form]]), equivalently when
$D\theta(z)^{\mathsf T}J\,D\theta(z)=J$ for the standard symplectic matrix
$J$ at every $z\in W_{0}$
([[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]]). A **canonical
chart of the presentation** is a chart whose coordinates are canonical in
this sense; the equivalence with the canonical maps defined later on this
page is recorded with those definitions.

**(b) The model's own charts are canonical.** The Cartesian coordinates
$(x,p)$ on $W$ are canonical coordinates: by clause 1 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] the two-form is
$\omega=\sum_{a}dx^{a}\wedge dp_{a}$. For a generalized-coordinate map, the
coordinates $(q,P)$ on $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ are canonical coordinates
for the pulled-back form $\omega_{X}$: by clause 2 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] one has
$\omega_{X}=\sum_{a}dq^{a}\wedge dP_{a}$, and when the map is a genuine chart
($r=3N$) the chart transition is a change of canonical coordinates on
overlaps.

**(c) Canonical one-form up to gauge.** The canonical one-form $\lambda$ of
[[def-cm13-two-form]] is said to be **in canonical form up to gauge** in the
canonical coordinates $\theta$ when the difference
$\lambda-\sum_{a}\theta^{m+a}d\theta^{a}$ is a closed one-form on $W_{0}$;
exactness of that difference is not required. For the presentation's own
charts the difference of the two canonical one-forms is closed by clause 3 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]].

**(d) Status and warnings.** The item defines a coordinate condition on a
declared chart and records the one fact that the presentation's own momentum
charts satisfy it. It asserts no existence of canonical coordinates beyond
the model's charts, no global statement on multiply connected phase domains,
no dynamics and no measured value. A chart that is merely a diffeomorphism
need not be canonical; the determinant test
$|\det D\theta|=1$ is necessary but, in dimension $2m\ge4$, not sufficient
for canonicity (the scope remark of this page records the witness).

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data and conventions of [[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]]: masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ and open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$,
a $C^{2}$ potential $U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing regularity
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]]). Dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]], the Euclidean product on $\mathbb R^{3N}$ is
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Write $n:=3N\ge1$. The
Cartesian momentum phase chart of the presentation is
$I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ with the momentum $p=\mathsf Mv$ of
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], and the momentum phase chart of a
generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates is
$I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ with the generalized momentum
$P=G(q)v$, $G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-hyperregularity]]).

**(a) Cartesian chart.** The **Cartesian phase domain of the presentation** is
the nonempty open set

$$W:=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n},\qquad z=(x,p),$$

a phase domain in the sense of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]
(openness is clause (a) of [[def-cm01-configuration]]). On $W$ the
**canonical one-form of the presentation in the Cartesian chart** is the smooth
one-form

$$\lambda_{(x,p)}(\delta x,\delta p):=p\cdot\delta x\qquad\bigl((x,p)\in W,\ (\delta x,\delta p)\in\mathbb R^{3N}\times\mathbb R^{3N}\bigr),$$

where $p\cdot\delta x$ is the Euclidean pairing of the momentum covector with
the displacement, and the **two-form of the presentation in the Cartesian
chart** is

$$\omega:=-d\lambda$$

([[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]). In coordinates, reading
$x=(x^{1},\dots,x^{3N})$ and $p=(p_{1},\dots,p_{3N})$ as the standard
coordinates of $W$,

$$\lambda=\sum_{a=1}^{3N}p_{a}\,dx^{a},\qquad \omega=\sum_{a=1}^{3N}dx^{a}\wedge dp_{a},\qquad \omega_{(x,p)}\bigl((\delta x,\delta p),(\delta x',\delta p')\bigr)=\delta x\cdot\delta p'-\delta p\cdot\delta x',$$

the last identity using the Euclidean product. The dimension of both forms is
that of action, $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$: the pairing of a momentum
($\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$) with a displacement ($\ell$). The forms have no
explicit time dependence; for each $t\in I_{0}$ the slice $\{t\}\times W$
carries the same two-form. The momentum phase chart with time,
$I_{0}\times W$ with coordinates $(t,x,p)$, is the domain of the Hamiltonians
and fields of this page. The **sign convention** fixed by
[[def-hamiltonian-vector-field-and-hamiltonian-function]] and used
throughout is $\iota_{X}\omega=dH$; $H$ denotes a phase function as in that
item.

**(b) Generalized-coordinate chart.** Let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be a
generalized-coordinate map with substituted Lagrangian $\widetilde L$ and
kinetic metric $G$, and let $r$ be its number of coordinates
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]). The **chart map of the
presentation in the coordinates $X$** is

$$\Phi_{X}:\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}\longrightarrow Q\times\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \Phi_{X}(q,P):=\Bigl(X(q),\ \mathsf M\,DX(q)\,G(q)^{-1}P\Bigr).$$

Here $DX(q)$ is the $(3N)\times r$ Jacobian of $X$ at $q$
([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), $G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$
is symmetric positive definite ([[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]],
[[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), and $P$ is a
generalized momentum. The image of $\Phi_{X}$ is

$$\Phi_{X}(\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r})=\bigl\{\,(X(q),\mathsf M\,DX(q)v)\ :\ q\in\Omega,\ v\in\mathbb R^{r}\,\bigr\},$$

the momentum chart of the presentation in the coordinates $X$; indeed
$P\mapsto v=G(q)^{-1}P$ is a linear bijection of $\mathbb R^{r}$. The map
$\Phi_{X}$ is $C^{1}$ by the displayed algebra, and it is a $C^{1}$ immersion:
its derivative is injective at every point, because $DX(q)$ is injective
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-euclidean-submersions-and-immersions]]) and $P\mapsto G(q)^{-1}P$ is a
linear bijection; when $r=3N$ its derivative is invertible and it is a local
diffeomorphism onto $W$
(equivalently $\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}=DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}$: see the
recorded identity below). The **forms of the presentation in the
coordinates $X$** are the pullbacks

$$\lambda_{X}:=\Phi_{X}^{*}\lambda,\qquad \omega_{X}:=\Phi_{X}^{*}\omega$$

([[def-pullback-of-a-differential-form]]). In the coordinates $(q,P)$ on
$\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ the following identities hold, and are proved in
clause 2 of the symplectic-structure theorem of this page:

$$\lambda_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}P_{a}\,dq^{a},\qquad \omega_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}dq^{a}\wedge dP_{a};$$

moreover, when $r=3N$ and $DX(q)$ is invertible,
$\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}=DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}$, so that on an open
generalized-coordinate chart the chart map reads
$\Phi_{X}(q,P)=\bigl(X(q),DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}P\bigr)$ and the chart
transition between the two descriptions of the same momentum datum is a
$C^{1}$ local diffeomorphism.

**(c) Status.** The item defines the two-form datum of the declared
presentation on its declared charts, together with the sign convention for
fields. It asserts no closedness, no nondegeneracy, no equation of motion, no
conservation law and no measured value; those are the subject of the other
items of this page. The forms depend on the declared chart and its coordinate
dimensions, but not on the residual forces $d$ nor on the normalization
$U\mapsto U+c(t)$ of the potential representative. All objects are model
objects of the idealization declared by the force branch.

derivations.claim: Clause 1 for the Hamilton system: by [F1] the hypotheses of [F2] are satisfied, so for every $\alpha$ close to $\alpha_{0}$ there is an open interval $I_{\alpha}\ni t_{0}$ and a $C^{1}$ curve $q:I_{\alpha}\to U$ with $q(t_{0})=q_{0}$, $q'=H_{p}(t,q,S_{q}(t,q,\alpha))$, and with $p:=S_{q}(t,q,\alpha)$ the pair $(q,p)$ solves $q'=H_{p}$, $p'=-H_{q}$ on $I_{\alpha}$.

Model reading of clause 1: on the potential branch $d\equiv0$ in the Cartesian chart, the curve $x:=q$ is $C^{1}$ with $x'=H_{p}$ and $p=S_{q}$; the first Hamilton equation reads $\mathsf M^{-1}p=x'$, so $p(t)=\mathsf Mx'(t)$, and clause 1 of [F3] upgrades $x$ to a $C^{2}$ motion of the model on $I_{\alpha}$. In a generalized-coordinate chart with $d\equiv0$, put $P:=p$; then $q'=\widetilde H_{P}$ and $P'=-\widetilde H_{q}$, and clause 3 of [F3] shows that $q$ solves the declared Lagrange equations and $P(t)=G(q(t))q'(t)$.

Clause 2: by [F2], $\beta(t)=S_{\alpha}(t,q(t),\alpha)$ is constant on $I_{\alpha}$ and equal to $S_{\alpha}(t_{0},q_{0},\alpha)$; the value $\beta_{0}=S_{\alpha}(t_{0},q_{0},\alpha_{0})$ is the labelled constant for the characteristic through the base point.

Clause 3: by [F2], the equation $\beta=S_{\alpha}(t,q,\alpha)$ is locally solvable for $q=Q(t,\alpha,\beta)$ near $(t_{0},\alpha_{0},\beta_{0})$, and the curve with $p=S_{q}(t,Q,\alpha)$ solves Hamilton's equations; the model reading is clause 1 of [F3] exactly as in step 2.1, now for the curve $Q$.

Clause 4: by [F2] the map $(q,p)\mapsto(\beta,\alpha)$ is a local diffeomorphism near the base point and $dq\wedge dp=d\beta\wedge d\alpha$ holds at fixed $t$ on its domain; by [F4] the chart coordinates $(q,p)$ are canonical for the presentation's two-form, so $\omega=\sum_{a}dq^{a}\wedge dp_{a}=dq\wedge dp$ there; substituting gives $\omega=d\beta\wedge d\alpha$, and [F4] identifies $(\beta,\alpha)$ as canonical coordinates of the presentation in the sense of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]]; the local diffeomorphism used here is the one established in step 3.1.
Collection: clauses 1-4 of the statement are steps 1.1, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1 and 4.1 respectively; this proves the statement.

boundaries.reason: The statement quantifies over declared nonempty open sets and one fixed base point; no possibly empty family is introduced (statement).

boundaries.evidence: Zero momentum and zero parameters are included: the argument never divides by $p=S_{q}$, only by $\det S_{q\alpha}\neq0$ (statement, step 1.1).
The one-pair case $m=1$ is included; all clauses are uniform in $m\ge1$ (statement, step 1.1).
The degenerate case $\det S_{q\alpha}=0$ is exactly what the complete-integral hypothesis excludes; the local converse is step 4.1 (statement).

boundaries.reason: No boundary-value problem is solved; the characteristic interval $I_{\alpha}$ is open and the converse is local near the base point (statement).
No selection principle is used: the local solution curve and the local inverses are supplied by the cited Picard-Lindelof and inverse-function theorems (steps 1.1 and 4.1).
The statement is a list of consequences of one complete integral, not an equivalence chain.
The local converse is a separate clause proved in step 4.1, not the reverse direction of an equivalence asserted in the statement.

citations.quote:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
the momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the
canonical coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]], the Hamiltonian fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] and the branch
Hamiltonian $H$ of [[def-cm12-hamiltonian]];
by clause 1 of [[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] each momentum phase
domain is a symplectic manifold for $\omega$, with $\omega$ the standard
two-form in the chart's canonical coordinates
([[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]). Dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]] and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) The datum.** Let $W_{0}$ be a nonempty open subset of one momentum
phase domain of the presentation, of dimension $2n$, and let

$$F=(F_{1},\dots,F_{n}),\qquad F_{i}:W_{0}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,$$

be phase functions of class $C^{\infty}$ with $F_{1}=H|_{W_{0}}$. The
family $F$ is a **completely integrable datum of the presentation on
$W_{0}$** when

1. $F$ is in involution, $\{F_{i},F_{j}\}=0$ on $W_{0}$ for all $i,j$
   ([[def-cm14-involution]] clause (d)); and
2. the differentials $dF_{1},\dots,dF_{n}$ are linearly independent on a
   dense open subset of $W_{0}$ ([[def-linear-independence]],
   [[def-differential-rank-and-constant-rank]]).

**(b) Reading in the root library.** Since $(W_{0},\omega)$ is a
$2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold and the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]] is the bracket of
[[def-poisson-bracket-on-a-symplectic-manifold]] for $\omega$, a datum
$F$ in the sense of clause (a), with $F_{1}=H$ and the autonomous
Hamiltonian $H$ of the presentation, is exactly a **completely integrable
Hamiltonian system** on $(W_{0},\omega)$ in the sense of
[[def-completely-integrable-hamiltonian-system]], with branches read
through the presentation's Hamiltonians; the root notion of
[[def-first-integral-and-poisson-commuting-functions]] is read through the
bracket criterion of [[pthm-cm13-observable-evolution]] clause 2.

**(c) Integral map, regular locus and fibres.** Attached to a datum $F$
are:

1. the **integral map** $F:W_{0}\to\mathbb R^{n}$;
2. the **regular locus** $W_{\mathrm{reg}}:=\{z\in W_{0}:
   \operatorname{rank}dF(z)=n\}$, which is open by continuity of the partial
   derivatives and dense in $W_{0}$ by clause (a) 2;
3. the **regular values**, namely the values $b\in F(W_{\mathrm{reg}})$;
   for such a value the **regular fibre** $N_{b}:=F^{-1}(b)$ is the
   common level set of $F_{1},\dots,F_{n}$ through $b$;
4. the **Hamiltonian fields** $X_{F_{1}},\dots,X_{F_{n}}$ of the family
   ([[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]).

**(d) Status.** The item defines a datum class and its attached objects.
It asserts that no particular model of the force branch is completely
integrable, that no fibre is compact, connected or a torus, that no
action-angle coordinates exist and no measured value is known; the
structural and motion statements are the torus theorem and the
action-angle theorem of this page (items `pthm-cm14-regular-tori` and
`pthm-cm14-action-angle`), conditional on the hypotheses stated there.

On a $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold, a Hamiltonian system is
**completely integrable** if it has smooth functions
$F_1=H,F_2,\ldots,F_n$ such that

1. $\{F_i,F_j\}=0$ for every $i,j$; and
2. $dF_1,\ldots,dF_n$ are linearly independent on a dense open subset.

The map $F=(F_1,\ldots,F_n):M\to\mathbb R^n$ is the **integral map**.
The set on which $dF$ has rank $n$ is its **regular locus**; it is open and,
by the preceding condition, dense.
Both involution and independence are essential. Results about regular fibres
apply only at regular values or specified regular components.

A smooth function $F$ is a **first integral** of a Hamiltonian $H$ if $F$ is
constant along every integral curve of $X_H$, on that curve's local maximal
domain. Functions $F_1,\ldots,F_k$ **Poisson commute** or are **in involution**
if $\{F_i,F_j\}=0$ for all $i,j$. The first definition does not presume that
the Hamiltonian flow is complete.

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
the momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the
Hamiltonian fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]] and the branch Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]]; the model reading of the Hamiltonian system is
the equivalence of [[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]]
(motions of the model are the integral curves of the branch Hamiltonian
field, in each chart with its own Hamiltonian). Dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]] and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Phase functions and the domain.** Let $W_{0}$ be a nonempty open
subset of one momentum phase domain of the presentation. A **phase
function of the presentation on $W_{0}$ of class $C^{k}$** is a map
$f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{k}$, of a declared dimension.

**(b) First integrals.** Let $f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{1}$.
Then $f$ is a **first integral of the branch Hamiltonian $H$ on $W_{0}$**
when for every interval $J\subseteq I_{0}$ with nonempty interior and every
solution $z:J\to W_{0}$ of the Hamiltonian system
$\dot z(t)=X_{H_{t}}(z(t))$
([[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]) the composite
$t\mapsto f(z(t))$ is constant on $J$. Equivalently, in the reading of
[[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]], $f$ is
constant along every motion of the model whose momentum-phase curve lies
in $W_{0}$ (on the potential branch).

**(c) The bracket criterion.** Let $H$ be autonomous on $I_{0}\times W_{0}$
($\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ and $d\equiv0$) and let $f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be
autonomous of class $C^{2}$. Then $f$ is a first integral of $H$ on $W_{0}$
if and only if

$$\{f,H\}=0\qquad\text{everywhere on }W_{0},$$

the bracket being that of [[def-cm13-poisson]]. The equivalence is clause
2 of [[pthm-cm13-observable-evolution]], recorded here as the working
form of the definition; it is not re-proved.

**(d) Involution.** Phase functions $f_{1},\dots,f_{k}:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$
of class $C^{2}$ are **in involution** (or **pairwise Poisson-commuting**)
when

$$\{f_{i},f_{j}\}=0\qquad\text{on }W_{0}\text{ for all }i,j\in\{1,\dots,k\};$$

a **family of first integrals in involution** is a family whose members are
first integrals of $H$ and which is in involution. The notion is the
presentation reading of the root-library notion of
[[def-first-integral-and-poisson-commuting-functions]] under the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]], which is the bracket of
[[def-poisson-bracket-on-a-symplectic-manifold]] for the two-form of
[[def-cm13-two-form]].

**(e) Differential independence.** Phase functions $f_{1},\dots,f_{k}$ of
class $C^{1}$ are **independent at $z\in W_{0}$** when the differentials
$df_{1}(z),\dots,df_{k}(z)$ are linearly independent as elements of the
dual of the tangent space at $z$ ([[def-linear-independence]]); the set
of points at which this holds is the **independence locus** of the family,
$\{z\in W_{0}:\operatorname{rank}(df_{1}(z),\dots,df_{k}(z))=k\}$
([[def-differential-rank-and-constant-rank]],
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]). The family is **independent on**
$W_{0}$ when it is independent at every $z\in W_{0}$.

**(f) Status.** The item defines model properties of phase functions and
records one proved equivalence from the evolution theorem of the
companion page. It asserts no existence of a nonconstant first integral
for a given force law, no completeness of any flow, no conservation law
of the model and no measured value; in particular every closure or
constancy statement about brackets is a theorem of this page or of
[[pthm-cm13-observable-evolution]], not part of the definition.

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the Hamiltonian
fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]], the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]] and the branch Hamiltonian $H$, assumed of class $C^{2}$
in $(t,z)$ on $I_{0}\times W$ ([[def-cm12-hamiltonian]],
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-configuration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be a nonempty open interval and
let $z:J\to W$ be a $C^{1}$ solution of the Hamiltonian system
$\dot z(t)=X_{H_{t}}(z(t))$, equivalently, on the potential branch with
$z=(x,p)$ and $p=\mathsf Mx'$, the momentum-phase curve of a motion of the
model ([[pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations]],
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]],
[[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]). Then:

1. **(evolution identity)** For every $C^{1}$ phase function
   $f:U\to\mathbb R$ on an open set $U$ containing the graph of $z$,
   $t\mapsto f(t,z(t))$ is differentiable on $J$ and

$$\frac{d}{dt}f\bigl(t,z(t)\bigr)=\partial_{t}f\bigl(t,z(t)\bigr)+\{f_{t},H_{t}\}\bigl(z(t)\bigr),$$

   where $f_{t}:=f(t,\cdot)$, $H_{t}:=H(t,\cdot)$ and the bracket is that of
   [[def-cm13-poisson]].
2. **(first integrals)** If $f$ is autonomous and
   $\{f,H_{t}\}(z(t))=0$ for every $t\in J$, then $f\circ z$ is constant on
   $J$; in particular, if in addition $H$ is autonomous
   ($\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ and $d\equiv0$), then $H$ itself is constant
   along $z$, the Hamiltonian form of the energy conservation of
   [[pthm-cm12-energy-time]].
3. **(closed algebra)** Let $H$ be autonomous and let $f,g$ be autonomous
   $C^{3}$ phase functions with $\{f,H\}=0$ and $\{g,H\}=0$ everywhere on
   their common domain. Then $\{f,g\}$ is again a first integral of $H$:
   $\{\{f,g\},H\}=0$ everywhere, and $\{f,g\}$ is constant along every
   solution of the Hamiltonian system on which it is defined.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared
presentation and the cited mathematics; it asserts no empirical content and
no existence, uniqueness or completeness of solutions.

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]] and the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]]: the Cartesian phase domain
$W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, its two-form $\omega$, a generalized-coordinate
chart map $\Phi_{X}$ and the form $\omega_{X}$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]); the presentation is
hyperregular on every chart with the Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] and [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]],

$$H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12\,p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x),\qquad \widetilde H(t,q,P)=\tfrac12\,P\cdot G(q)^{-1}P+\widetilde U(t,q).$$

Differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], and gradients those of
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]].

**(a) The field of a phase function.** Let $W_{0}\subseteq W$ be nonempty
open and let $f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{2}$. By clause 1 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] the form $\omega$ is nondegenerate on
$W_{0}$, so there is exactly one $C^{1}$ vector field $X_{f}$ on $W_{0}$ with

$$\iota_{X_{f}}\omega=df$$

(the sign convention of [[def-hamiltonian-vector-field-and-hamiltonian-function]]
and [[prop-cm-hamiltonian-field-and-poisson-bracket-in-a-phase-chart]]); it
is the **Hamiltonian field of $f$ for the presentation**. In the Cartesian
coordinates $(x,p)$, writing $\nabla f=(f_{x^{1}},\dots,f_{x^{3N}},f_{p_{1}},\dots,f_{p_{3N}})$,

$$X_{f}=\bigl(f_{p},\,-f_{x}\bigr)=J\nabla f,\qquad J=\begin{pmatrix}0_{3N}&I_{3N}\\-I_{3N}&0_{3N}\end{pmatrix};$$

in any canonical chart $(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m})$ of the presentation
the same field reads $X_{f}=\bigl(f_{\theta^{m+1}},\dots,f_{\theta^{2m}},-f_{\theta^{1}},\dots,-f_{\theta^{m}}\bigr)$.
A vector field on $W_{0}$ is called **Hamiltonian for the presentation** when
it is $X_{f}$ for some $C^{2}$ function $f$; in particular
$X_{f}=0$ exactly when $f$ is locally constant on $W_{0}$. Vector fields are
read as tangent-bundle sections of
[[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]].

**(b) The field of the branch Hamiltonian.** For each $t\in I_{0}$ the
function $H_{t}:=H(t,\cdot)$ is $C^{2}$ on $W$, and the **Hamiltonian field
of the presentation** at time $t$ is $X_{H_{t}}$:

$$X_{H_{t}}(x,p)=\bigl(\mathsf M^{-1}p,\ -\nabla_{x}U(t,x)\bigr),$$

whose components are a velocity and a force. In the coordinates $X$ the
corresponding field is
$X_{\widetilde H_{t}}(q,P)=\bigl(G(q)^{-1}P,\ -\partial_{q}\widetilde H(t,q,P)\bigr)$,
where the second slot retains the kinetic contribution
$-\tfrac12P\cdot\partial_{q}(G(q)^{-1})P$ when the metric varies. If
$d\not\equiv0$ the model's forced evolution carries the additional momentum
source $d$; the corresponding vector field
$(x,p)\mapsto\bigl(\mathsf M^{-1}p,-\nabla_{x}U(t,x)+d(t,x,\mathsf M^{-1}p)\bigr)$
is generally not a Hamiltonian field for the presentation, and it is one
exactly when the residual force has a potential independent of the velocity
slot (the criterion is proved in clause 4 of the corresponding theorem of this
page).

**(c) Time dependence and status.** For a time-dependent $H$ the assignment
$t\mapsto X_{H_{t}}$ is a time-dependent field on the phase domain; each
$X_{H_{t}}$ is $C^{1}$, hence locally Lipschitz in the state variable, and no
completeness of its integral curves is asserted here. The item defines the
field datum and its chart expressions; the identification of the model's
motions with the integral curves, and all conservation or invariance
properties, are the subject of the other items of this page. The field is
defined by the intrinsic equation $\iota_{X}\omega=dH$ and therefore does not
depend on the canonical chart used to compute it.

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]] and the Hamiltonian fields of
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]. Dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]];
differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Phase functions.** Let $W_{0}$ be a nonempty open subset of a phase
domain of the presentation. A **phase function of the presentation on
$W_{0}$ of class $C^{k}$** is a map $f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{k}$
($k\ge1$); its physical reading is a model quantity computed from the
positions and momenta of the labels, and its dimension is declared as part of
the datum. A **time-dependent phase function** on an interval $J\subseteq
I_{0}$ is a map $f:J\times W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ of the declared class, written
$f_{t}:=f(t,\cdot)$.

**(b) The bracket.** Let $f,g:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{2}$. By
[[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] the fields $X_{f},X_{g}$ are defined on
$W_{0}$, and the **Poisson bracket of $f$ and $g$ for the presentation** is
the phase function

$$\{f,g\}:=\omega(X_{f},X_{g})=d\!f(X_{g})=X_{g}(f)=-X_{f}(g),$$

the sign convention being that of
[[def-poisson-bracket-on-a-symplectic-manifold]] and
[[prop-cm-hamiltonian-field-and-poisson-bracket-in-a-phase-chart]]; the
bracket is $C^{1}$ on $W_{0}$ and its dimension is
$[f]\,[g]\,(\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1})^{-1}$, the product of the dimensions of the
entries divided by the action dimension of the two-form.

**(c) Coordinate formula.** In the Cartesian canonical coordinates $(x,p)$
of the presentation, and more generally in any canonical chart
$(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m})$ of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]],

$$\{f,g\}=\sum_{a=1}^{3N}\Bigl(f_{x^{a}}g_{p_{a}}-f_{p_{a}}g_{x^{a}}\Bigr)=\nabla f^{\mathsf T}J\,\nabla g,\qquad \{f,g\}=\sum_{a=1}^{m}\Bigl(f_{\theta^{a}}g_{\theta^{m+a}}-f_{\theta^{m+a}}g_{\theta^{a}}\Bigr),$$

with derivatives those of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. The coordinate formula is
recorded here and its identities (bilinearity, skew-symmetry, the Leibniz
rule, the Jacobi identity and the fundamental brackets) are proved in the
bracket-identities theorem of this page.

**(d) Status.** The item defines a bilinear operation on the declared phase
domain by the intrinsic formula $\{f,g\}=\omega(X_{f},X_{g})$, hence
independently of the canonical chart used to evaluate the coordinate
formula. It asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law, no algebraic
identity beyond well-definedness and no measured value; in particular the
bracket with the Hamiltonian and the notion of first integral are the subject
of the evolution theorem of this page.

For $F,G\in C^\infty(M)$, the **Poisson bracket** in the library convention is

$$\{F,G\}:=\omega(X_F,X_G)=dF(X_G)=X_G(F)=-X_F(G).$$

All four formulas use $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$. In particular, the order in the
observable formula is important: evolution by $H$ differentiates $F$ as
$X_H(F)=\{F,H\}$.

For $H\in C^\infty(M)$, its **Hamiltonian vector field** is the vector field
$X_H$ determined by the library sign convention

$$\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH.$$

A vector field $X$ is **Hamiltonian** if $\iota_X\omega=dH$ for some smooth
function $H$; such an $H$ is a **Hamiltonian function for $X$**. A function and
its vector field are distinct data, and completeness of $X_H$ is not assumed.

A **symplectic form** on a smooth manifold $M$ is a smooth two-form $\omega$
such that

1. $d\omega=0$, and
2. $(T_pM,\omega_p)$ is a [[def-symplectic-vector-space|symplectic vector
   space]] for every $p\in M$.

The pair $(M,\omega)$ is a **symplectic manifold**. Thus both closedness and
pointwise nondegeneracy are required. A zero-dimensional manifold with its
zero two-form satisfies the definition.

Let $F:M^m\to N^n$ be smooth, let $q\in N$ be a regular value, and assume
$F^{-1}(q)$ is nonempty. Then $F^{-1}(q)$ is an embedded submanifold of
codimension $n$. Equivalently, it has dimension $m-n$.

Let $m,n\ge 1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). The **rank of $f$ at $a\in U$** is
$$\operatorname{rank}_a f:=\operatorname{rank}Df(a),$$
where rank is the dimension of the image ([[def-rank-and-nullity]]). In the standard bases, this is also the rank of the Jacobian matrix $Jf(a)$ ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]).

For $S\subseteq U$ and $0\le r\le\min\{m,n\}$, the map $f$ has **constant rank $r$ on $S$** when $\operatorname{rank}Df(x)=r$ for every $x\in S$. On the empty set this condition is vacuous, so it may hold for more than one $r$; every assertion that needs a determined rank will assume $S$ is nonempty or specify $r$.

For a completely integrable system
$F=(F_1,\ldots,F_n)$ on a $2n$-manifold, every nonempty regular common level
$N=F^{-1}(c)$ is an $n$-dimensional Lagrangian submanifold. At each point,

$$T_pN=\operatorname{span}\{X_{F_1}(p),\ldots,X_{F_n}(p)\}.$$

On the regular locus of a completely integrable system, the fields
$X_{F_1},\ldots,X_{F_n}$ integrate to a local $\mathbb R^n$-action. On a
compact invariant regular fibre their restrictions are complete, so the action
is global on that fibre.

This item assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, namely [[def-countable-choice|countable choice]]. In the propagated dependency chain, that assumption is required through [[cor-every-smooth-vector-field-on-a-compact-manifold-is-complete]]; after those interfaces are fixed, the remaining local or finite argument makes no additional countable-family choice.

On a compact connected regular fibre $N$ of a completely integrable system,
the $\mathbb R^n$-action is transitive. Its stabilizer $\Gamma$ is a discrete
full lattice in $\mathbb R^n$, and $N\cong\mathbb R^n/\Gamma$.

This item assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, namely [[def-countable-choice|countable choice]]. In the propagated dependency chain, that assumption is required through [[lem-stabilizer-of-the-r-n-action-on-a-compact-connected-regular-fibre-is-a-full-lattice]]; after those interfaces are fixed, the remaining local or finite argument makes no additional countable-family choice.

Every compact connected regular fibre of a completely integrable system on a
$2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold is diffeomorphic to the torus
$T^n=\mathbb R^n/\mathbb Z^n$.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Every smooth vector field on a compact manifold is complete.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Clause 1: by [F3] and the hypotheses, $N$ is a nonempty compact connected embedded submanifold of dimension $n$, and it is a regular common level of the completely integrable system [F1] read on $(W_{0},\omega)$ by [F2]; clause 1 of [F4] therefore makes $N$ a Lagrangian submanifold and gives the displayed spanning of its tangent spaces by the Hamiltonian fields.

Clause 2, commuting fields: clause 2 of [F4] gives that the fields $X_{F_{1}},\dots,X_{F_{n}}$ pairwise commute and that their flows combine into a local $\mathbb R^{n}$ action; each $X_{F_{i}}$ is tangent to $N$ because $dF_{j}(X_{F_{i}})=\{F_{j},F_{i}\}=0$ on $N$ for every $j$, and $N$ is a common level set.

Clause 2, completeness and lattice: $N$ is compact by hypothesis, so on it each restricted field is complete by the completeness result of [F4]; under $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ from [A1], the lattice lemma of [F4] then states that the action on the compact connected regular fibre $N$ is transitive with the same full stabilizer lattice $\Gamma\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$ at every point and that $N\cong\mathbb R^{n}/\Gamma$.
Clause 3: the torus theorem of [F4] gives that the compact connected regular fibre $N$ is diffeomorphic to $T^{n}=\mathbb R^{n}/\mathbb Z^{n}$.
Collection: clause 1 is step 1.1, clause 2 is steps 2.1 and 3.1, and clause 3 is step 4.1; this proves the statement.

boundaries.evidence: The fibre $N$ is assumed nonempty; empty fibres are excluded by hypothesis (statement).

boundaries.reason: No numerical quantity with a distinguished zero value occurs; the fibre point ranges over the compact manifold $N$.

boundaries.evidence: $n=1$ is included: the cited structural results hold for every $n\ge1$ and the one-dimensional fibre is a circle (statement, step 1.1).
Degenerate fibres are excluded by the regularity of the value: $dF$ has rank $n$ on $N$ (statement, step 1.1).

boundaries.reason: $N$ is a compact manifold without boundary and no endpoint case occurs (statement).

boundaries.evidence: ACω is assumed in the statement and used exactly through the cited lattice lemma in step 3.1.

boundaries.reason: The statement is a list of conclusions about the fibre, not an equivalence chain.
No reverse implication is asserted; the proper-submersion hypothesis is used only by the action-angle theorem of the same page.

citations.quote:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
the momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]], the
canonical coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]], the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]], the Hamiltonian fields of [[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]] and the branch
Hamiltonian $H$ of [[def-cm12-hamiltonian]];
by clause 1 of [[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] each momentum phase
domain is a symplectic manifold for $\omega$, with $\omega$ the standard
two-form in the chart's canonical coordinates
([[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]). Dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]] and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) The datum.** Let $W_{0}$ be a nonempty open subset of one momentum
phase domain of the presentation, of dimension $2n$, and let

$$F=(F_{1},\dots,F_{n}),\qquad F_{i}:W_{0}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,$$

be phase functions of class $C^{\infty}$ with $F_{1}=H|_{W_{0}}$. The
family $F$ is a **completely integrable datum of the presentation on
$W_{0}$** when

1. $F$ is in involution, $\{F_{i},F_{j}\}=0$ on $W_{0}$ for all $i,j$
   ([[def-cm14-involution]] clause (d)); and
2. the differentials $dF_{1},\dots,dF_{n}$ are linearly independent on a
   dense open subset of $W_{0}$ ([[def-linear-independence]],
   [[def-differential-rank-and-constant-rank]]).

**(b) Reading in the root library.** Since $(W_{0},\omega)$ is a
$2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold and the bracket of
[[def-cm13-poisson]] is the bracket of
[[def-poisson-bracket-on-a-symplectic-manifold]] for $\omega$, a datum
$F$ in the sense of clause (a), with $F_{1}=H$ and the autonomous
Hamiltonian $H$ of the presentation, is exactly a **completely integrable
Hamiltonian system** on $(W_{0},\omega)$ in the sense of
[[def-completely-integrable-hamiltonian-system]], with branches read
through the presentation's Hamiltonians; the root notion of
[[def-first-integral-and-poisson-commuting-functions]] is read through the
bracket criterion of [[pthm-cm13-observable-evolution]] clause 2.

**(c) Integral map, regular locus and fibres.** Attached to a datum $F$
are:

1. the **integral map** $F:W_{0}\to\mathbb R^{n}$;
2. the **regular locus** $W_{\mathrm{reg}}:=\{z\in W_{0}:
   \operatorname{rank}dF(z)=n\}$, which is open by continuity of the partial
   derivatives and dense in $W_{0}$ by clause (a) 2;
3. the **regular values**, namely the values $b\in F(W_{\mathrm{reg}})$;
   for such a value the **regular fibre** $N_{b}:=F^{-1}(b)$ is the
   common level set of $F_{1},\dots,F_{n}$ through $b$;
4. the **Hamiltonian fields** $X_{F_{1}},\dots,X_{F_{n}}$ of the family
   ([[def-cm13-hamiltonian-field]]).

**(d) Status.** The item defines a datum class and its attached objects.
It asserts that no particular model of the force branch is completely
integrable, that no fibre is compact, connected or a torus, that no
action-angle coordinates exist and no measured value is known; the
structural and motion statements are the torus theorem and the
action-angle theorem of this page (items `pthm-cm14-regular-tori` and
`pthm-cm14-action-angle`), conditional on the hypotheses stated there.

On a $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold, a Hamiltonian system is
**completely integrable** if it has smooth functions
$F_1=H,F_2,\ldots,F_n$ such that

1. $\{F_i,F_j\}=0$ for every $i,j$; and
2. $dF_1,\ldots,dF_n$ are linearly independent on a dense open subset.

The map $F=(F_1,\ldots,F_n):M\to\mathbb R^n$ is the **integral map**.
The set on which $dF$ has rank $n$ is its **regular locus**; it is open and,
by the preceding condition, dense.
Both involution and independence are essential. Results about regular fibres
apply only at regular values or specified regular components.

A **symplectic form** on a smooth manifold $M$ is a smooth two-form $\omega$
such that

1. $d\omega=0$, and
2. $(T_pM,\omega_p)$ is a [[def-symplectic-vector-space|symplectic vector
   space]] for every $p\in M$.

The pair $(M,\omega)$ is a **symplectic manifold**. Thus both closedness and
pointwise nondegeneracy are required. A zero-dimensional manifold with its
zero two-form satisfies the definition.

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
data, charts and forms of [[def-cm13-two-form]]: masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$,
open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ and mass operator
$\mathsf M$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]), time window $I_{0}$, $C^{2}$
potential $U$ and residual forces $d$ of the standing regularity
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]],
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], [[def-cm01-units]]), the Cartesian phase
domain $W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ with $n=3N$, its canonical one-form
$\lambda$ and two-form $\omega=-d\lambda$, and for each generalized-coordinate
map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates and kinetic metric $G$ the chart map
$\Phi_{X}(q,P)=(X(q),\mathsf M\,DX(q)G(q)^{-1}P)$ with pullbacks
$\lambda_{X}=\Phi_{X}^{*}\lambda$ and $\omega_{X}=\Phi_{X}^{*}\omega$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], [[def-cm12-hyperregularity]]). Then:

1. **(Cartesian chart)** $\omega$ is the standard two-form of the phase
   domain $W$ in the sense of
   [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]: $d\omega=0$ and
   $\omega$ is nondegenerate at every point of $W$; hence $(W,\omega)$ is a
   symplectic manifold in the sense of
   [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]].
2. **(generalized-coordinate chart)** On $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$,

$$\lambda_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}P_{a}\,dq^{a},\qquad \omega_{X}=\sum_{a=1}^{r}dq^{a}\wedge dP_{a};$$

   consequently $\omega_{X}$ is closed and nondegenerate at every point, so
   $\Phi_{X}^{*}\omega$ is the standard two-form of the phase domain
   $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ and $\Phi_{X}$ preserves the two-form.
3. **(chart independence)** Where two of the presentation's charts are
   defined and overlap, the transition between them preserves the two-form,
   and the difference of their canonical one-forms is closed: any two
   momentum charts of the presentation describe the same symplectic
   structure on the overlap, up to the closed one-form $\lambda$ gauge.

The statement is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the
declared presentation and the cited mathematics. It asserts no equation of
motion, no conservation law, no completeness of any flow and no empirical
content.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,\omega)$
be a symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, let $F=(F_1,\dots,F_n)$ be a completely integrable
system on $M$ ([[def-completely-integrable-hamiltonian-system]]) and let $N=F^{-1}(b_0)$ be a
nonempty compact connected regular fibre. Assume that, after restricting to a saturated
neighbourhood $U$ of $N$ and a ball $B\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ of regular values with $F(U)=B$, the map
$\pi:=F|_U:U\to B$ is a proper submersion with connected fibres. Then, after shrinking $B$ to a
smaller ball $B'$ and $U$ to $\pi^{-1}(B')$, there are action-angle coordinates
$(I,\theta):U\to B'\times T^n$ in the sense of [[def-action-and-angle-coordinates]] (period-one
angles) with

$$\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n d\theta_i\wedge dI_i ,$$

and every $C^\infty$ function on $U$ that is constant on the fibres of $\pi$ (in particular each
$F_i$) is a function of $I$ alone.

**Action–angle coordinates** on a neighbourhood $U$ fibred by Lagrangian
tori are a diffeomorphism

$$ (I,\theta):U\longrightarrow B\times(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^n,$$

where $B\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is open, such that the components
$I=(I_1,\ldots,I_n)$ and
$\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)$ have fibres $I=\mathrm{constant}$ and

$$\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n d\theta_i\wedge dI_i.$$

This page uses period one for every angle. Replacing angles by period $2\pi$
rescales the corresponding actions and formulas. The order
$d\theta_i\wedge dI_i$ is forced by the library convention
$\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$: it gives $\dot\theta_i=\partial H/\partial I_i$.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U$ be a phase domain with standard two-form
$\omega_U=\sum_i dq^i\wedge dp_i$ ([[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]]), and let
$H:U\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^2$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Write
$\nabla H=(H_{q^1},\dots,H_{q^n},H_{p_1},\dots,H_{p_n})$ for the Euclidean gradient
([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]) and $J$ for the standard symplectic matrix. Then:

1. there is exactly one $C^1$ vector field $X_H$ on $U$ with $\iota_{X_H}\omega_U=dH$, and it is
   $$X_H=J\nabla H=\bigl(H_{p_1},\dots,H_{p_n},-H_{q^1},\dots,-H_{q^n}\bigr);$$
2. an integral curve $t\mapsto(q(t),p(t))$ of $X_H$ satisfies Hamilton's equations
   $$\dot q^i=H_{p_i}(q,p),\qquad \dot p_i=-H_{q^i}(q,p)\qquad(i=1,\dots,n);$$
3. for $f,g\in C^2(U)$ the Poisson bracket
   $\{f,g\}:=\omega_U(X_f,X_g)$ ([[def-poisson-bracket-on-a-symplectic-manifold]]) is
   $$\{f,g\}=\nabla f^{\mathsf T}J\,\nabla g=\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(f_{q^i}g_{p_i}-f_{p_i}g_{q^i}\bigr),$$
   hence $\{f,g\}=-\{g,f\}$, and $\{f,g\}$ is $C^1$ on $U$.

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with the
momentum charts and two-form datum of [[def-cm13-two-form]] and the canonical
coordinates of [[def-cm13-canonical-form]]: the Cartesian phase domain
$W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, its two-form $\omega$, a generalized-coordinate
chart map $\Phi_{X}$ and the form $\omega_{X}$
([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]); the presentation is
hyperregular on every chart with the Hamiltonian $H$ of
[[def-cm12-hamiltonian]] and [[pthm-cm12-mechanical-hyperregularity]],

$$H(t,x,p)=\tfrac12\,p\cdot\mathsf M^{-1}p+U(t,x),\qquad \widetilde H(t,q,P)=\tfrac12\,P\cdot G(q)^{-1}P+\widetilde U(t,q).$$

Differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], and gradients those of
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]].

**(a) The field of a phase function.** Let $W_{0}\subseteq W$ be nonempty
open and let $f:W_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{2}$. By clause 1 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] the form $\omega$ is nondegenerate on
$W_{0}$, so there is exactly one $C^{1}$ vector field $X_{f}$ on $W_{0}$ with

$$\iota_{X_{f}}\omega=df$$

(the sign convention of [[def-hamiltonian-vector-field-and-hamiltonian-function]]
and [[prop-cm-hamiltonian-field-and-poisson-bracket-in-a-phase-chart]]); it
is the **Hamiltonian field of $f$ for the presentation**. In the Cartesian
coordinates $(x,p)$, writing $\nabla f=(f_{x^{1}},\dots,f_{x^{3N}},f_{p_{1}},\dots,f_{p_{3N}})$,

$$X_{f}=\bigl(f_{p},\,-f_{x}\bigr)=J\nabla f,\qquad J=\begin{pmatrix}0_{3N}&I_{3N}\\-I_{3N}&0_{3N}\end{pmatrix};$$

in any canonical chart $(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m})$ of the presentation
the same field reads $X_{f}=\bigl(f_{\theta^{m+1}},\dots,f_{\theta^{2m}},-f_{\theta^{1}},\dots,-f_{\theta^{m}}\bigr)$.
A vector field on $W_{0}$ is called **Hamiltonian for the presentation** when
it is $X_{f}$ for some $C^{2}$ function $f$; in particular
$X_{f}=0$ exactly when $f$ is locally constant on $W_{0}$. Vector fields are
read as tangent-bundle sections of
[[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]].

**(b) The field of the branch Hamiltonian.** For each $t\in I_{0}$ the
function $H_{t}:=H(t,\cdot)$ is $C^{2}$ on $W$, and the **Hamiltonian field
of the presentation** at time $t$ is $X_{H_{t}}$:

$$X_{H_{t}}(x,p)=\bigl(\mathsf M^{-1}p,\ -\nabla_{x}U(t,x)\bigr),$$

whose components are a velocity and a force. In the coordinates $X$ the
corresponding field is
$X_{\widetilde H_{t}}(q,P)=\bigl(G(q)^{-1}P,\ -\partial_{q}\widetilde H(t,q,P)\bigr)$,
where the second slot retains the kinetic contribution
$-\tfrac12P\cdot\partial_{q}(G(q)^{-1})P$ when the metric varies. If
$d\not\equiv0$ the model's forced evolution carries the additional momentum
source $d$; the corresponding vector field
$(x,p)\mapsto\bigl(\mathsf M^{-1}p,-\nabla_{x}U(t,x)+d(t,x,\mathsf M^{-1}p)\bigr)$
is generally not a Hamiltonian field for the presentation, and it is one
exactly when the residual force has a potential independent of the velocity
slot (the criterion is proved in clause 4 of the corresponding theorem of this
page).

**(c) Time dependence and status.** For a time-dependent $H$ the assignment
$t\mapsto X_{H_{t}}$ is a time-dependent field on the phase domain; each
$X_{H_{t}}$ is $C^{1}$, hence locally Lipschitz in the state variable, and no
completeness of its integral curves is asserted here. The item defines the
field datum and its chart expressions; the identification of the model's
motions with the integral curves, and all conservation or invariance
properties, are the subject of the other items of this page. The field is
defined by the intrinsic equation $\iota_{X}\omega=dH$ and therefore does not
depend on the canonical chart used to compute it.

In action–angle coordinates, if $H=h(I)$ then

$$\dot I_i=0,\qquad \dot\theta_i=\frac{\partial h}{\partial I_i},\qquad \theta(t)=\theta(0)+t\nabla h(I(0))\pmod{\mathbb Z^n}.$$

For $H\in C^\infty(M)$, its **Hamiltonian vector field** is the vector field
$X_H$ determined by the library sign convention

$$\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH.$$

A vector field $X$ is **Hamiltonian** if $\iota_X\omega=dH$ for some smooth
function $H$; such an $H$ is a **Hamiltonian function for $X$**. A function and
its vector field are distinct data, and completeness of $X_H$ is not assumed.

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] with the
momentum charts, the phase domains and the two-form datum of
[[def-cm13-two-form]]: the Cartesian phase domain $W=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
with $n=3N$, its two-form $\omega$, and for each generalized-coordinate map
$X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r$ coordinates the chart map $\Phi_{X}$ and the form
$\omega_{X}$ ([[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]],
[[def-cm12-cotangent-momentum]], [[def-cm01-configuration]]). All
differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Canonical coordinates.** Let $W_{0}\subseteq W$ (or
$W_{0}\subseteq\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$) be nonempty open, and let

$$\theta=(\theta^{1},\dots,\theta^{2m}):W_{0}\longrightarrow V\subseteq\mathbb R^{2m}$$

be a $C^{1}$ chart of $W_{0}$ onto an open set $V$ ([[def-metric-topology]]),
with $m$ the half-dimension of $W_{0}$. The coordinates $\theta$ are
**canonical coordinates for the presentation's two-form** on $W_{0}$ when the
two-form takes the **canonical form**

$$\omega=\sum_{a=1}^{m}d\theta^{a}\wedge d\theta^{m+a}$$

on $W_{0}$ ([[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]); equivalently, when the
pullback identity $\theta^{*}\omega_{V}^{\mathrm{st}}=\omega|_{W_{0}}$ holds
for the standard two-form $\omega_{V}^{\mathrm{st}}$ of $V$
([[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]],
[[def-pullback-of-a-differential-form]]), equivalently when
$D\theta(z)^{\mathsf T}J\,D\theta(z)=J$ for the standard symplectic matrix
$J$ at every $z\in W_{0}$
([[prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport]]). A **canonical
chart of the presentation** is a chart whose coordinates are canonical in
this sense; the equivalence with the canonical maps defined later on this
page is recorded with those definitions.

**(b) The model's own charts are canonical.** The Cartesian coordinates
$(x,p)$ on $W$ are canonical coordinates: by clause 1 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] the two-form is
$\omega=\sum_{a}dx^{a}\wedge dp_{a}$. For a generalized-coordinate map, the
coordinates $(q,P)$ on $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}$ are canonical coordinates
for the pulled-back form $\omega_{X}$: by clause 2 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]] one has
$\omega_{X}=\sum_{a}dq^{a}\wedge dP_{a}$, and when the map is a genuine chart
($r=3N$) the chart transition is a change of canonical coordinates on
overlaps.

**(c) Canonical one-form up to gauge.** The canonical one-form $\lambda$ of
[[def-cm13-two-form]] is said to be **in canonical form up to gauge** in the
canonical coordinates $\theta$ when the difference
$\lambda-\sum_{a}\theta^{m+a}d\theta^{a}$ is a closed one-form on $W_{0}$;
exactness of that difference is not required. For the presentation's own
charts the difference of the two canonical one-forms is closed by clause 3 of
[[pthm-cm13-two-form-is-symplectic]].

**(d) Status and warnings.** The item defines a coordinate condition on a
